rationale: Evidence from iteration 0: all 60 development trials went off track (ended_by off_track: 20/20 on each track). Progress was only 0.05 to 0.13, so no run finished. Every run had 2 line-loss events, which means the robot lost the tape early and never recovered. max_error was about 0.06 to 0.068 m, right at the off-track limit of 0.0625 m, and rms_error was about 0.025 to 0.029 m. Steering oscillation was moderate (about 0.15). The likely cause is over-aggressive steering at high speed: kp = 4 gives up to 1400 PWM of differential for a full-scale signal, and kd = 0.1 is too weak to damp the swing. The robot overshoots across the line, loses it, and drifts off. Changes: (1) kp 4.0 to 2.5, to halve the steering gain and reduce overshoot. (2) kd 0.1 to 0.3, to add damping against the fast signal changes. (3) base_speed 1.8 to 1.6, to give the controller more time to correct on bends. The trade-off is a slower lap, so completion_time may rise, but staying on track matters more while the robot fails early. Geometry is unchanged so that the controller change is the only variable. Expected result: line_loss_events fall to 0 or 1, progress rises well above 0.13, and at least some runs complete. Hypotheses to test: (H1) the early off-track is caused by overshoot, so line_loss_events should drop with lower kp; (H2) with the line held, progress should reach at least 0.5 on the oval; (H3) if the runs still leave the track, the problem is sensor geometry or the line-loss response rather than gains. Next measurements to check: completion, progress, completion_time, line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation. If the runs now stay on track but do not finish within 3 s, raise base_speed toward 2.0. If oscillation is still high, lower kp further or raise kd.
